templates.name: Auto-Remediate macOS Endpoints via Jamf Pro
templates.description: Auto-remediates Critical and High SVM vulnerabilities on Macs by adding the affected device to the Static Computer Group that already scopes the app's deployment in Jamf. Supports BOTH deployment surfaces: Jamf App Catalog (App Installers - for Firefox, Chrome, Zoom, etc.) and Mac App Store (Mac Apps - for Apple's apps, Slack from App Store, etc.). Fully dynamic discovery - no group ids, group names, or deployment ids hardcoded. notification_email is the only customer knob. Flow: SRT fires -> find Mac by asset name -> try App Catalog first (list deployments, match by name, extract smartGroup.id) -> if no match, fall back to Mac App Store (list, match, fetch detail for scope) -> fetch Smart Group criteria -> resolve Static Group by name -> PUT device into Static Group -> mark CVE IN_PROGRESS. Jamf evaluates the cascade and pushes the install on next agent check-in (~15 min). SentinelOne agent auto-resolves the CVE on next scan. Customer Jamf prerequisites: 1. Add the app from EITHER Jamf App Catalog (preferred for third-party) OR Mac App Store. Keep Jamf's default name - the workflow matches by name containing SVM software.name (case-insensitive). 2. Set the deployment's target to a Smart Computer Group with a 'Computer Group: member of, <some Static Group>' criterion. The Static Group can be named anything; the workflow follows the cascade. 3. Required API role privileges: Read Computer Inventory Collection, Read Computers, Read Mac Applications, Read Smart Computer Groups, Read Static Computer Groups, Update Static Computer Groups. Plus a SentinelOne xSPM API key. Limitations: - Supports the 'app deployment -> Smart Group -> Static Group cascade' pattern only. Installomator/Patch Policy customers need a different template. - Substring name match picks the first hit (App Catalog checked first). Avoid duplicate-named entries. - Lists fetched with page-size=200; customers with more deployments may miss matches.

templates.name: Auto-Remediate Windows Mac and Linux Endpoints via Manage Engine
templates.description: Auto-remediates Critical and High SVM vulnerabilities by triggering the latest applicable patch deployment in ManageEngine Patch Manager Plus. Looks up the affected endpoint in PMP, identifies the newest matching missing patch by software vendor, approves it, and installs it using the PMP tenant's default deployment policy. Marks the SVM vulnerability IN_PROGRESS; the SentinelOne agent auto-resolves it on next scan. Covers Windows OS + 3rd-party, macOS OS + 3rd-party, and Linux packages - single graph, no OS-specific branching.

templates.name: Auto-Remediate Windows Mac and Linux Endpoints via NinjaOne
templates.description: Auto-remediates Critical and High SVM vulnerabilities on endpoints managed by NinjaOne. Single graph covers Windows, macOS, and Linux for BOTH OS updates AND third-party app updates. SRT fires; workflow looks up the device via /v2/devices/search, classifies which patch surface to hit based on the device's OS and the SVM software.type, and queues the apply via /v2/device/{id}/patch/{os|software}/apply. Marks the CVE IN_PROGRESS; the SentinelOne agent auto-resolves on next scan. Classification: - Linux device -> always /patch/os/apply. On Linux, both OS updates AND third-party apps flow through the OS patch surface via local apt/yum repos. /patch/software/* intentionally 400s on Linux by NinjaOne's design. - Windows/macOS AND software.type == 'OS' -> /patch/os/apply. - Windows/macOS AND software.type != 'OS' -> /patch/software/apply. Apply API takes no body and no per-patch targeting - it queues ALL pending approved patches for that surface. Customer's NinjaOne agent policy (approval rules, severity filters) fully controls what installs. Customer NinjaOne prerequisites: 1. Endpoints enrolled with NinjaOne agent (Windows, macOS, or Linux). 2. Agent policy with the right patching options enabled per OS: Windows/macOS need Software Patching enabled (separate toggle from OS Patching). Linux needs the master 'Enable patching' toggle on, plus the third-party app's vendor repository configured on the device (e.g. Chrome's apt source in /etc/apt/sources.list.d/). 3. Approval rules auto-approving at the severity you want auto-remediated. 4. API Client (Administration -> Apps -> API) with scopes Monitoring + Management, grant type Client Credentials. 5. SentinelOne xSPM API token for the final status update. Notes: - macOS App Store apps: patchable via /patch/software/apply, but once patched they update through NinjaOne, not the App Store. - Device search uses score==100 exact-name match; keep hostnames unique.

templates.name: Automated Threat Hunting with AlienVault OTX
templates.description: This workflow retrieves indicators of compromise (IOCs) from recent security reports and searches for them in SentinelOne's Singularity Data Lake. When matches are identified, incidents are automatically created to ensure timely response. The workflow streamlines the threat detection process, allowing security teams to quickly address potential threats and reduce response times.
steps: Schedule Pulse Retrieval: Automatically pull Threat Pulses from AlienVault every 3 hours to ensure the latest threat intelligence is available.
Iterate Over Pulses: For each Threat Pulse received, iterate through the list of indicators of compromise (IOCs) to assess potential threats.
Search for Matching Events: For each IOC, search SentinelOne's Singularity Data Lake for matching events that occurred in the last 14 days to identify potential incidents.

Create or Update Issues: For each IOC with matching events, create a new issue or add a comment to an existing issue if the IOC is already associated with it. This ensures all relevant information is consolidated for efficient incident management.
Documentation and Notification: Document all actions and update relevant stakeholders with the latest status on incident handling to maintain transparency and facilitate collaboration.

templates.name: Configure AWS CloudFormation Stack to send Notifications
templates.description: This template remediates the lack of visibility into CloudFormation stack events by configuring an Amazon SNS (Simple Notification Service) topic to receive stack notifications. It performs the following actions: 1. Accepts User Input for the Topic ARN 2. Updates the stack to associate it with the specified SNS Topic ARN. This ensures that any events related to the stack (such as CREATE_IN_PROGRESS, UPDATE_COMPLETE, or ROLLBACK_FAILED) trigger a notification to the subscribed endpoints (email, SMS, Lambda, etc.), allowing for real-time monitoring of infrastructure changes. Configuration Required SNS Topic ARN: You must provide the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the existing SNS topic where stack events will be published (e.g., arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:MySecurityAlerts). Required Permissions To execute this remediation, the automation role requires the following AWS permissions: 1. cloudformation:UpdateStack Validating permissions Ensure that the role that was created while onboarding your cloud account has these permissions to successfully execute the remediation workflow. To validate, login to your cloud account and check the assigned permissions to the role that was created while onboarding your cloud account or Organization. If there are missing permissions, edit the onboarded cloud account or Organization from Policy & Settings and rerun the deployment template to enable CNS assume role with new permissions. Cost Implications Low. There is no cost for the configuration change itself. However, standard Amazon SNS pricing applies for any actual notifications published to the topic (e.g., costs per million requests or per SMS sent). Review the template before activating it.

templates.name: LLM Cookbook 1 - The Router
templates.description: RECIPE: split the decision from the explanation. A constrained `llm` action returns one word from a closed vocabulary so a Condition can branch on it deterministically; a second `llm` action writes the human rationale for the alert note. Anything the router does not emit cleanly falls through to a fail-closed default that changes no alert state and asks for a human. Trigger is on-demand (run_automatically=false) - flip it once you trust the routing on your own alert mix.

templates.name: LLM Cookbook 10 - The Tribunal
templates.description: RECIPE: two models in tension with a typed hand-off, and a gate the workflow can count. The critic receives the proposal field by field and returns typed objections; the workflow counts BLOCKING ones itself and only asks a human to approve a proposal that survived. The v1 synthesis call is gone: the brief is rendered from both objects.

templates.name: LLM Cookbook 2 - The Extractor
templates.description: RECIPE: the prompt is the schema. With response_format=off the only output contract is the one you write in the prompt - so make the model emit your TARGET API's enum (IPV4/DNS/SHA256...) directly. The loop then posts each indicator to the Threat Intelligence API with zero type-mapping logic, because the type field is already correct. Paste any incident report, advisory or phishing email into the trigger. Note the negative instructions: an extractor that never says 'no indicators' is an extractor that invents them, so the schema has an `excluded` array to give the model somewhere honest to put what it dropped.

templates.name: LLM Cookbook 3 - The Renderer
templates.description: RECIPE: never pipe markdown into an email. Mail clients render none of it, so a one-shot 'analyse and format as HTML' prompt gives you either a wall of ## and ** or a shallower analysis - the model spends its attention on presentation. Split it: pass 1 reasons in markdown with no presentation constraints at all, pass 2 is a pure format transform that is explicitly forbidden from changing any claim. The raw markdown is archived on the alert as the audit trail; only the rendered fragment reaches the inbox.

templates.name: LLM Cookbook 4 - The Analyst
templates.description: RECIPE: the LLM as the 'so what?' layer over a query result. The PowerQuery already answers 'what' - the expensive human step is ranking 25 rows by what deserves attention today, and that is the job worth giving a model. Two things make it work: hand over the SCHEMA (`columns`) alongside the ROWS (`values`) and explain that the format is column-oriented, because a model given a bare 2D array guesses at what the columns mean; and fence off what the data cannot support - one snapshot with no baseline cannot show a trend, so the prompt forbids trend language outright. Uses the synchronous /sdl/api/powerQuery, which is safe here only because the query is a capped aggregate; for anything returning bulk rows switch to an async LRQ launch-and-poll.

templates.name: LLM Cookbook 5 - The Advocate
templates.description: RECIPE: two models in tension, then a fail-closed approval gate delivered by email. A single call asked to 'propose and critique' defends its own work, so the critique gets its own call with an adversarial brief and no authorship to defend - and is explicitly allowed to concede. The synthesis step returns JSON FIELDS rather than prose, and the email template owns the layout: that removes the console's 200-character cap on an interaction form description, keeps rendering identical every run, and stops model output from deciding the structure of your HTML. Every field is read through Function.DEFAULT (an absent key errors the run) wrapped in Function.HTML_ENCODE (the value lands inside HTML). Approval uses a `choice` interaction, which mints one URL per option and renders as two buttons. The gate FAILS CLOSED: the remediation branch needs result equals 'Authorise Remediation' AND timeout equals false, so an ignored email declines.

templates.name: LLM Cookbook 6 - The Gatekeeper
templates.description: RECIPE: enums + integers make branching deterministic and keep policy in the workflow. One strict LLM call returns a route enum, an integer confidence and typed evidence; Conditions test route with equals and confidence with a numeric threshold. Anything below threshold fails closed to human review. On-demand trigger; flip to automatic once trusted.

templates.name: LLM Cookbook 7 - The Harvester
templates.description: RECIPE: an array of objects you can loop over directly. The schema's enum is the Threat Intelligence API's type vocabulary and ttl_hours is an integer the workflow does arithmetic on, so each item drops straight into the IOC payload. The report email is rendered by jq and counted with LENGTH: no second LLM call, no model-reported counts.

templates.name: LLM Cookbook 8 - The Composer
templates.description: RECIPE: the model reasons, the workflow renders. One strict call fills a nested analysis object; two jq templates turn the same object into a branded HTML email and a plain-text alert note. Markdown leakage is impossible because the model never controls layout.

templates.name: LLM Cookbook 9 - The Dispatcher
templates.description: RECIPE: a typed boolean silences quiet mornings, nested id arrays route work back to the right alerts. A daily sweep clusters and ranks open HIGH/CRITICAL alerts; the workflow verifies every model-supplied id against the input before writing a note. Strict guarantees the shape, not the truth.

templates.name: SOCRadar Alert Enrichment
templates.description: Enriches the file hash of new Medium, High and Critical alerts with the SOCRadar IOC Enrichment API and writes the risk score, malware verdict and whitelist status as a note on the alert. Prerequisites - SOCRadar connection using your SOCRadar IOC Enrichment API key (Api-Key header, the default). - SentinelOne GraphQL connection: a service user whose role has Alerts - View, including endpoint alerts (unifiedAlerts:view, unifiedAlerts:viewEndpointAlerts). Admin is not required. Steps in this template 1. Read the SHA256 (or SHA1) file hash from the alert; alerts without a file hash are skipped. 2. Query SOCRadar IOC Enrichment for the hash. A first query for a hash SOCRadar does not hold yet returns 404 and starts a lookup, so the request retries once after 10 seconds. 3. Add the SOCRadar score, malware categorization, whitelist status and VirusTotal link as an alert note.

This key is separate from the IOC Enrichment key. - SentinelOne GraphQL connection: a service user whose role has Alerts - View, including endpoint alerts (unifiedAlerts:view, unifiedAlerts:viewEndpointAlerts). Admin is not required. Steps in this template 1. Read the SHA256 (or SHA1) file hash from the alert; alerts without a file hash are skipped. 2. Query SOCRadar Rapid Reputation for the hash. 3. Add the reputation score (0-100, higher is worse) and whitelist status as an alert note.

templates.name: SOCRadar Threat Feed Ingestion
templates.description: Every 12 hours, pulls the indicators of your subscribed SOCRadar threat feed collections and submits them to Singularity Threat Intelligence in batches of 100 indicators per request. Prerequisites - SOCRadar connection using your SOCRadar Threat Feed API key. The Threat Feed API only accepts the key as a URL parameter: set the connection's way to pass to URL parameters with the name key. - SentinelOne connection: the Add IOCs to Threat Intelligence step uses the SentinelOne Add IOCs action, which requires the console permissions threatIntelligence:manage and threatIntelligence:view (Threat Intelligence - Manage). Give the connection's service user a role with these; Admin is not required. - In Set Parameters, list your collections in collections (uuid, name, ioc_type, severity) and set site-id to the site that receives the indicators. Steps in this template 1. For each collection, fetch its indicators from SOCRadar. 2. Build the Threat Intelligence IOC records with Function.JQ and split them into batches of batch-size (default 100). 3. Submit each batch with one POST /web/api/v2.1/threat-intelligence/iocs request. Indicators expire after ioc-valid-hours (default 168, 7 days) unless the next pull refreshes them. ioc_type must match the collection: hash collections use MD5, SHA1 or SHA256, ip collections IPV4 or IPV6, hostname collections DNS and url collections URL. A loop runs at most 10,000 iterations, so one collection can hold up to 1,000,000 indicators at the default batch size.

templates.name: Specify Protocol for AWS EC2 Security Group Inbound Rules
templates.description: This template remediates security groups that allow all traffic (Protocol "-1") by restricting them to a specific port and protocol defined by the user. It performs the following specific steps: 1. User Input: Prompts the user to specify the desired safe Protocol (e.g., "tcp") and Port (e.g., "443"). 2. Discovery: Retrieves all rules for the target Security Group. 3. Remediation Loop: Iterates through the rules to identify Inbound rules allowing "All Protocols". 4. Atomic Update: Modifies the identified rules to enforce the user's specified Protocol and Port, while strictly preserving the original Source (IP Range or Security Group ID) to prevent connectivity loss. Required Permissions To execute this remediation, the automation role requires the following AWS permissions: 1. ec2:DescribeSecurityGroupRules 2. ec2:ModifySecurityGroupRules Validating permissions Ensure that the role that was created while onboarding your cloud account has these permissions to successfully execute the remediation workflow. To validate, login to your cloud account and check the assigned permissions to the role that was created while onboarding your cloud account or Organization. If there are missing permissions, edit the onboarded cloud account or Organization from Policy & Settings and rerun the deployment template to enable CNS assume role with new permissions. Cost Implications None.
steps: Prompts the user to specify the desired safe Protocol (e.g., "tcp") and Port (e.g., "443").
Discovery: Retrieves all rules for the target Security Group
Remediation Loop: Iterates through the rules to identify Inbound rules allowing "All Protocols".

Atomic Update: Modifies the identified rules to enforce the user's specified Protocol and Port, while strictly preserving the original Source (IP Range or Security Group ID) to prevent connectivity loss.
